sentence.paragraph_en: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
sentence.paragraph_zh: 为了探究这一问题，我们向15个月大的婴儿展示两种情形中的一种：一名实验者努力工作以实现两个不同的目标，或者一名毫不费力地实现每个目标的实验者。随后，我们向婴儿介绍一个新颖的音乐玩具，看起来似乎可以通过按下顶部的大按钮来启动。这个按钮可以被按下，但实际上并不会启动任何功能。在婴儿看不见的地方，我们用一个隐藏按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具发出音乐。我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开房间。之后，不知道每个婴儿属于哪种实验条件的分析人员观看了实验录像，并统计婴儿试图通过按下按钮启动玩具的次数。

sentence.text: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
sentence.zh: 如果经营B&B的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在贸然投入这项业务之前，有几个因素需要考虑。首先要考虑的是你的房产，不仅包括建筑物本身，还包括其位置。如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或住在纽约市、华盛顿特区等热门目的地，你的房子即使相当普通，也仍然可以很好地经营成B&B。另一方面，如果你的房屋在建筑风格上独具特色，或拥有方便旅行者使用的设施，例如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意走相当远的路来投宿。另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。你必须考虑家庭的每一位成员是否真的喜欢接待客人，是否愿意反复谈论当地的景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力承担由此增加的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。最后还要考虑财务因素。潜在的B&B经营者必须现实地看待收入机会。虽然B&B通常前期成本较低，但专家估计，经营者至少需要定期出租五间客房，才能靠B&B维持生计。

sentence.paragraph_en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.

sentence.paragraph_en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.

sentence.text: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others.
sentence.zh: 这项针对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有群体都遵循七项基本的道德准则。这些普遍规则是：帮助家人，帮助群体，回报他人的帮助，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，以及尊重他人的财产。研究人员发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者群体，还是先进文明，各类社会都重视这些品格；这些品格有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。“每个地方的每个人都拥有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说，“这七条道德规则之所以在不同文化中都具有普遍性，是因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即便其中一些品格看起来属于右翼或保守立场，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会表现出对某个群体的忠诚，以及对某个人或某种事物的服从。这表明，真正将我们联结在一起的因素多于分裂我们的因素。”

sentence.paragraph_en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."

sentence.paragraph_en: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships; they do not differ in this respect. However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come. Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature; girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises. Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.

sentence.paragraph_en: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships; they do not differ in this respect. However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come. Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature; girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises. sentence.paragraph_en: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main." Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self", and not even our bodies are truly "us".

sentence.paragraph_en: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there. The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures. Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top. The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer. Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.

sentence.text: But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.

Another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife who was behind the wheel.

sentence.paragraph_en: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. sentence.text: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.

sentence.paragraph_en: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul. Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return. So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day. Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. And collecting that cash is serious business. Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain. In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them. Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

sentence.text: When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.
sentence.zh: 一组美国研究人员比较了学生在有背景语音、器乐或一般噪声的环境中阅读时对文字材料的理解情况。一般噪声是中性的，例如空调或风扇发出的声音。在有背景语音的情况下，学生的得分下降幅度最大。有音乐时的理解效果略好于有语音时。然而，当要求学生辨认旋律而不是理解文字时，背景音乐的干扰更大。当背景语音使用参与者不熟悉的语言时，对阅读理解几乎没有妨碍，或者说妨碍很小。

sentence.paragraph_en: A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music or general noise. General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan. Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more. When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.
sentence.paragraph_zh: 一组美国研究人员比较了学生在有背景语音、器乐或一般噪声的环境中阅读时对文字材料的理解情况。一般噪声是中性的，例如空调或风扇发出的声音。在有背景语音的情况下，学生的得分下降幅度最大。有音乐时的理解效果略好于有语音时。然而，当要求学生辨认旋律而不是理解文字时，背景音乐的干扰更大。当背景语音使用参与者不熟悉的语言时，对阅读理解几乎没有妨碍，或者说妨碍很小。

sentence.paragraph_en: Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core. Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond. However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctual responses coming from the primitive brain. As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior.

sentence.paragraph_en: These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence. The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time. Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts. sentence.text: And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness.
sentence.zh: 之所以会因未能实现目标而感到恼怒，问题在于目标总是在变化，而我们也始终在不断调整自己，无论是否意识到这一点。因此，最终我们会觉得自己永远不可能实现目标。这正是人们对失败、不满和不幸福最大的误解和原因之一。我们总是拿自己与目标进行比较，而不是与过去的自己比较。Dan Sullivan 将此称为“差距与收获”。我们总是以目标为参照进行衡量，而我们从未觉得自己正在接近目标；我们没有衡量收获，也就是自己从何处走来。衡量自己从何处走来，而不是试图走向何方时，我们就能看到成果。我们会看到那些曾经视为理所当然或未曾注意到的事情。这是观念上的一个简单却深刻的改变，而我喜欢它的地方在于，它所拥有的力量能够让我们立刻提升一个层次。它非常非常简单，却能立即对我们的思维产生积极影响。

sentence.paragraph_en: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we're never going to reach our goals. And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness. We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. Dan Sullivan calls this "the gap and the gain". We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we've come from. In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. We see things we've taken for granted, or not noticed. It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear. It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

sentence.paragraph_en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 °C in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through. sentence.paragraph_en: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something. In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture. Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad. sentence.paragraph_en: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul. Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return. So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day. Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. And collecting that cash is serious business. Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain. In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them. Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

sentence.paragraph_en: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul. Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return. So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day. Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. And collecting that cash is serious business. Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain. In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them. Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

sentence.paragraph_en: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories. They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time. In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted. But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
sentence.paragraph_zh: 尽管气味唤回的记忆具有特殊性，但它们也存在与其他记忆相同的缺陷。它们并不总是准确的，而且会随着时间发生变化。事实上，每当我们回忆某件事时，那段记忆都有可能被扭曲。但是，由于这些记忆唤起了强烈的情感联系，那些因某种气味而回忆起某件事的人往往坚信自己的记忆是准确的，即使事实并非如此。

sentence.paragraph_en: Despite the huge investment into research, ageing remains somewhat obscure, although there are certain things researchers do understand. They know that women tend to have longer lifespans, living on average six years longer than men. No one is really certain of the reason for this, although the speculation centers around the idea that women are more capable of surviving or handling disease than men. For virtually every disease, the effects are greater on men than they are on women.

sentence.paragraph_en: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools. While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products. When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors. But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer. It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year. Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants. Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions. By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."

sentence.text: Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness.
sentence.zh: 现在，我们来看看压力如何有益于身体。这对普通人来说可能令人意外。但专家表示，压力可以使你不易生病。科学家承认，长期压力会使人更容易患病。但研究表明，短时间的压力实际上能够提供一定的防病保护，因为它会增强免疫功能。一项研究显示，经历短暂压力的大鼠，其免疫细胞反应会激增，从而使免疫系统更好地准备对抗疾病。对于人类，甚至有证据表明，在接种疫苗前经历压力可能有助于提高疫苗的有效性。

sentence.paragraph_en: Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body. This may come as a surprise to laymen. But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick. Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness. But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning. One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness. For humans, there's even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.

sentence.paragraph_en: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there. The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures. Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top. The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer. Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.
sentence.paragraph_zh: 冰箱门内侧的那些小格子虽然很方便，但无法保持恒定的温度，所以一定不要把易腐食品放在那里。冰箱顶部区域没有底部那么冷，因此应留给那些不需要特别低温的食物。把即食食品或已经烹调好的食物放在顶层搁板上。如果顶部没有空间，也可以把饮料和熟食放在中层搁板上。中层搁板是冰箱内温度控制最稳定的区域，因此应把鸡蛋放在这里。底层搁板靠后的部位是冰箱内最冷的地方，所以应把易腐乳制品存放在这里，以便延长其可食用时间。切勿在这里存放含水量高的食物，因为其中的水分会结冰，从而彻底毁掉这些食物。

sentence.paragraph_en: As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction. If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal free. That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them. sentence.paragraph_en: In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your senses are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous and spontaneous. Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively. These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses. When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. This way you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability.

sentence.zh: 我们应当为自己的身份以及所代表的群体感到自豪。然而，当我们认为自己的群体或信仰比身边的人更好时，自豪感开始转变为优越感，我们就开始形成可能造成伤害的偏见态度。例如，一个群体的偏见态度可能使另一个群体无法进入某些学校、无法居住在自己想住的任何社区，或者无法获得工作或晋升。极端的偏见情绪曾导致无辜者死亡。我们应当为自己的思想和看法负责。当我们让别人告诉自己应当如何看待某个人或某件事时，我们就放弃了对自己生活的一部分掌控权。

sentence.paragraph_en: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent. If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful. For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion. Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people. We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions. When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
sentence.paragraph_zh: 我们应当为自己的身份以及所代表的群体感到自豪。然而，当我们认为自己的群体或信仰比身边的人更好时，自豪感开始转变为优越感，我们就开始形成可能造成伤害的偏见态度。例如，一个群体的偏见态度可能使另一个群体无法进入某些学校、无法居住在自己想住的任何社区，或者无法获得工作或晋升。极端的偏见情绪曾导致无辜者死亡。我们应当为自己的思想和看法负责。当我们让别人告诉自己应当如何看待某个人或某件事时，我们就放弃了对自己生活的一部分掌控权。

sentence.paragraph_en: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems? There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution. One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position. The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace. Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.

sentence.text: This is the illusion I seek to tackle.

sentence.paragraph_en: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity. "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes. "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have an unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you. This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us."

sentence.paragraph_en: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors. Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom, and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish. Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing and reacting. Those changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.

sentence.text: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
sentence.zh: 这项针对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有群体都遵循七项基本的道德准则。这些普遍规则是：帮助家人，帮助群体，回报他人的帮助，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，以及尊重他人的财产。研究人员发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者群体，还是先进文明，各类社会都重视这些品格；这些品格有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。“每个地方的每个人都拥有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说，“这七条道德规则之所以在不同文化中都具有普遍性，是因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即便其中一些品格看起来属于右翼或保守立场，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会表现出对某个群体的忠诚，以及对某个人或某种事物的服从。这表明，真正将我们联结在一起的因素多于分裂我们的因素。”

sentence.paragraph_en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."

sentence.text: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a "social ladder", representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career.
sentence.zh: 一项新研究考察了在财务资源背景下意义与幸福之间的关系。多伦多大学的里娅·卡塔帕诺及其同事发现，对于富裕人群而言，意义是幸福感的预测因素，其作用远弱于对较贫困人群的作用，这表明经济资源可能会影响我们体验意义的方式。研究团队分析了来自123个国家的50多万人的数据。第一项研究使用了2013年至2015年间收集的美国居民每日民意调查数据。研究人员通过积极情绪指标追踪幸福感，即调查前一天，参与者是否曾多次微笑或大笑，或体验到很强的幸福感。意义感则通过每日的“目标指数”进行测量，该指数考察参与者在多大程度上觉得自己喜欢每天所做的事情，并且有动力实现自己的目标。最后，研究人员评估了收入水平。结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在收入较低的人群中最强。但随着收入水平提高，这种相关性逐渐减弱。第二项研究考察了全球数据。幸福感采用与第一项研究相同的问题进行测量，而意义感则通过一个单一问题进行测量：“你是否觉得自己的生活具有重要的目标或意义？”同样，意义与幸福之间关系的强弱取决于参与者的收入：与收入较高的人群相比，意义对低收入人群幸福感的影响更大。在最后一项研究中，法国参与者表明了自己在多大程度上觉得过着有目标且有意义的生活，以及他们在多大程度上认为自己是一个幸福的人。最后，他们没有按照具体收入阶层进行划分，而是将自己置于一架“社会阶梯”上，以代表自己在社会中就财富、教育和职业而言所处的位置。该研究的结果与前两项研究的结果一致。
sentence.zh_type: 原句所在段的参考译文
